name: The Mr. T Experience
label: Lookout!
lede: In 1985 Frank Portman started a Berkeley band named after Mr. T's merchandise. Ten other members came and went, the band spent the 1990s and early 2000s on Lookout!, and in 2006 Portman published a novel.

eras.title: The name is a joke about 1985
eras.text: Portman and Stamatatos had a high school band; in 1985 they find two more players in Berkeley and name the new one after a TV tough guy's product line. The first records come out on other people's labels, and one of those labels folds.

years.big: Just another in the long line of products.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience · Wikipedia: Frank Portman
years.h: The band is named for the year Mr. T was on everything
years.p: Frank Portman, a.k.a. [[Dr. Frank|9c7174de-8941-422f-a17b-9ae9d14dc534]], starts the band in Berkeley in summer 1985 with Byron Stamatatos, Jon von Zelowitz and Alex Laipenieks. Portman's reasoning: Mr. T had products all over the place, so this would be the punk rock one.
years.xp:
Portman and Stamatatos had played together in a high school band, the Bent Nails, in Millbrae. In Berkeley they met Zelowitz, a university DJ, and Laipenieks, a high school friend of Portman's brother.

Portman later joked about the name: "One of our records, the title was 'Too Late to Change the Name.'"

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: A debut recorded and mixed in a single day
years.p: Everybody's Entitled to Their Own Opinion comes out in July 1986. Wikipedia credits Disorder Records; Encyclopedia.com calls it self-released.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says it was recorded and mixed in one day in July and "went for tunefulness rather than overall quality." Lookout! reissued it in 1995.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Night Shift at the Thrill Factory goes out on Rough Trade
years.p: The second album is released on the UK indie label's American arm. Around now Portman starts introducing songs on stage with "this song is about a girl."
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com dates the album to 1987 and counts 17 songs, produced with Kent Steedman of the Celibate Rifles. It calls the record faster, harder and more love-minded than the debut.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Rough Trade folds right after the Big Black Bugs Bleed Blue Blood EP
years.p: The EP appears in 1989 and Rough Trade shuts down shortly after, leaving the band without a label.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says the seven-song EP includes an ode to "Gilman Street," the Berkeley club the band came up in. The band's next label would be Lookout!.

years.h: Aaron Rubin takes over on bass from Byron Stamatatos
years.p: Stamatatos, Portman's friend from the Bent Nails, steps out. Rubin is the bassist when the band signs to Lookout!.

eras.title: Lookout! moves in
eras.text: A young Berkeley label signs the band and keeps it for the rest of its Lookout! run. The first records fans still play come out here, along with the first European tour.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Making Things with Light becomes Lookout!'s first CD
years.p: Portman's vocals move to the front and the rhythm guitars step back on the band's first Lookout! album.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says the band got there "by pushing the vocals to the forefront and placing the rhythm guitars in a more supportive role," and names "What Went Wrong" as the leading track.

years.big: Often overlooked, failing to figure prominently into the punk rock genealogy.
years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Lookout! signs the band after Rough Trade folds
years.p: Encyclopedia.com's verdict on a band that stayed with Lookout! for its whole run and played its style nearly a decade before Green Day and Rancid got huge.
years.xp: The band came up in the Gilman Street scene alongside Operation Ivy and Green Day. After Rough Trade closed in 1989 there was no label to go back to; Lookout! was where they landed, and Wikipedia says they stayed through their whole career.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Milk Milk Lemonade follows a first trip to Europe
years.p: The tour included recording the live EP Strum ünd Bang, Live!? in Spain.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com calls the album "another giant step forward in musical complexity," with vocals and guitars entwined more skillfully and more diversity than before.

years.h: Jon von Zelowitz quits, and the band almost goes with him
years.p: He leaves after getting back from the first European tour. A brief reunion attempt does not hold, and the band carries on as a trio.
years.xp: Zelowitz had contributed significantly to the early songwriting. Encyclopedia.com says he went on to the Rip Offs.

eras.title: Musical chairs
eras.text: Laipenieks won't tour, Rubin keeps leaving for Samiam, and Portman thinks about graduate school. Jym Pittman and Joel Reader end up as the new rhythm section.

years.h: As a trio, the band cuts Gun Crazy, then Our Bodies Our Selves
years.p: Portman, Rubin and Laipenieks record the EP first and the album after.
years.xp: Laipenieks then declined to tour and left, which brought another near-breakup. Portman considered graduate school and Rubin joined Samiam. Jim "Jym" Pittman took over on drums.

years.h: Alex Laipenieks won't tour, so Jym Pittman takes the drums
years.p: Pittman, who stays for two decades, comes in for the original drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience · Encyclopedia.com
years.h: Rubin returns for ...And the Women Who Love Them
years.p: Wikipedia says the EP gave the group new creative energy.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com describes the trio as relaunching itself as a pure pop-punk outfit with the release.

years.h: Our Bodies, Our Selves turns calmer and folkier
years.p: Encyclopedia.com calls it the calmer, more folk-influenced record, one that put Portman's songwriting out front.

years.h: Rubin goes back to Samiam, and a longtime fan takes his bass
years.p: Joel Reader, who has been playing along to the band's records since age 11, takes over on bass. The trio with Portman and Pittman lasts four years.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says Reader met Portman at Gilman Street and joined as a teenager.

eras.title: A record a year
eras.text: Portman, Reader and Pittman put out an album a year and get songs into a Ben Affleck movie and a Disney TV film. It's the steadiest lineup the band has had since the late 1980s.

years.cap: The band at a Winnipeg tour stop, spring 1996 (c. 1996)
years.h: Kevin Army produces Love Is Dead, the new trio's first album
years.p: Out January 19, 1996, recorded in 1995 at Bay Records and Emeryville Recording Company.
years.xp:
Trouser Press, quoted on Wikipedia, called it "a wonderful album," and Metroactive named it "the year's can't-miss record." Ira Robbins wrote that Portman's "grimsmirk spirit infects the whole wonderful album."

One track, Somebody's Song, sets a poem by Dorothy Parker. Artwork is by Christopher Appelgren and Portman.

years.h: "I Just Wanna Do It With You" lands in Glory Daze
years.p: The 1996 college comedy with Ben Affleck also uses "Even Hitler Had a Girlfriend" and the band's cover of "Now We Are Twenty-One."

years.h: One original member left, and he calls it the MTX Starship
years.p: By Revenge Is Sweet, and So Are You, Frank Portman is the last original member and jokes about the rotating crew accordingly.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com calls the album "another bubblegum-punk album" and says Portman had used the joke name for the rotating lineup.

years.h: Side band the Bomb Bassets release Take a Trip
years.p: Portman and Dallas Denery record as the Bomb Bassets, with the album out July 29, 1997.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Joel Reader joined the Bomb Bassets that year, with Dallas and John Denery, Kevin Army and Jym Pittman.

years.h: The band records Road to Ruin, a full tribute to the Ramones
years.p: The Ramones are its biggest influence. A song from 1998, She's Coming (Over Tonight), plays in a record store scene in Disney's My Date with the President's Daughter.

years.h: Fourth album in four years, and a solo record on the side
years.p: Alcatraz comes out in 1999 alongside Frank Portman's solo album Show Business Is My Life.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says Alcatraz includes bits of roller-rink organ, with songs like Two of Us and We're No One.

years.h: Joel Reader steps out, Gabe Meline steps in on bass
years.p: Organist Erik Noyes also plays with the band from 1999 to 2000.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Meline had already contributed to the Alcatraz recording. Noyes had played on earlier recordings but toured officially only in summer 1999.

eras.title: Quieter, then four again
eras.text: Touring gets sporadic and the bassist leaves. By 2003 the band is a four-piece for the first time in ten years.

years.h: A Miracle of Shame EP with an organ on it
years.p: Gabe Meline's last record with the band, made with Erik Noyes on organ as a semi-official member.

years.h: Gabe Meline leaves after a stretch of sporadic touring
years.p: Bobby J Jordan takes the bass in 2003.

years.h: Ted Angel and Bobby J Jordan make the band a four-piece again
years.p: Jordan takes over on bass and Angel adds guitar, the first four-piece in ten years. Portman's solo EP Eight Little Songs also appears.

years.h: Yesterday Rules is the band's last album on Lookout!
years.p: Touring afterward is limited, and by 2005 the band is mostly inactive while Portman writes.

eras.title: Dr. Frank, novelist
eras.text: Portman writes a novel about a teenage record nerd, and the band mostly goes quiet. It comes back with a new drummer, a sequel and an album you get by buying a book.

years.cap: Frank Portman at Bottom of the Hill, San Francisco
years.src: Wikipedia: Frank Portman · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Portman's first novel, King Dork, hits shelves
years.p: The novel about a teenage record nerd is optioned by Gary Sanchez Productions, with Sony Pictures later involved. The band goes quiet after 2005.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the film option came in November 2006. The band's own rule of thumb, in Portman's words: "deep meaning and content doesn't belong in rock'n'roll music."

years.h: Second novel, Andromeda Klein
years.p: It comes out in 2009, three years after King Dork.

years.h: Jaz Brown takes the drums after Jym Pittman's two decades
years.p: Brown joins Portman, Angel and Jordan.

years.h: Eight years after King Dork, the sequel
years.p: King Dork Approximately is published in December 2014. Portman plays Nostalgia Fest the same year.

years.cap: The band live on the 2019 tour with the Queers
yt: Ba Ba Ba Ba Ba, live, Nov. 10, 2017
years.h: The eleventh album comes with a book
years.p: King Dork Approximately: The Album came out October 24, 2016, available only by buying the reprinted novel, which carries a download code. Shards Vol. 1 arrives the same year.
years.xp: Shards Vol. 2 follows in 2017 and Vol. 3 in 2021, each collecting further new songs. The album is based on the King Dork books.

years.h: Alex Laipenieks, the original drummer, dies
years.p: Wikipedia lists the year as 2021 and gives no cause. He had left the band in 1993 rather than tour.
